title: Who's Who: Hugo Fenwick
summary: Chronometer maker whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Hugo Fenwick (1820–1870) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a chronometer maker whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Fenwick built paired clocks for the 1858 return-discrepancy trials, sealing one in the expedition case and retaining its twin in the laboratory. Their disagreements were small enough to invite accusations of faulty springs but consistent enough to change field procedure.
His clocks now have separate ordinary and expedition service records.

For Alderwick readers, Hugo Fenwick is remembered not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
